_comment: Copy to prepublish.config.json and fill in YOUR names, then run:
uv run python scripts/prepublish_gate.py
The gate REFUSES TO RUN without prepublish.config.json rather than scanning with these
placeholders. A gate that reads clean because nobody configured it is worse than no gate:
it produces a confident PASS over a repo nobody checked. That failure mode has cost this
project real time, which is why it fails loudly instead.
Universal rules live in the script itself and need no configuration: vendor credential
shapes (sk-, ghp_, xox*-, EAA…, re_, PEM blocks) and hosting identifiers (Supabase project
refs, *.fastapicloud.dev origins). What you declare here is what is specific to YOU.
Patterns are Python regex, matched case-INSENSITIVELY.
⚠️ Use a LEADING \b but NOT a trailing one on names: `_` is a word character, so
`\bacme\b` does NOT match `acme_prod` — and a brand id with a suffix is exactly the
spelling that slips through. Measured here, not theorised.
⚠️ These placeholders deliberately do NOT include the bundled Acme example brand.
Acme IS the template's public example — declaring it protected makes a fresh clone fail
with 88 findings on its own documentation, which teaches a new user that the gate cries
wolf. Measured on 2026-09-24 by doing exactly that. Replace these with YOUR names and the
gate goes from passing-because-empty to actually guarding something.
no_ship_files: individual files inside a shipping directory that must NOT ship —
e.g. your own persona or brand examples sitting beside the generic one. They stay
TRACKED, so the advisory keeps listing them: excluded from the export, never invisible.
brands: REPLACE ME — your brand id / name
prefixes: REPLACE ME — your live env prefix
identifiers: REPLACE ME — hosting team / account name
